This game has a lot of combat, but with most weapons you can't aim and dodge at the same time, and your ship is 10X more powerful than the enemies anyway, so there's little point in even trying to dodge. Just exchange hits and grind to get better gear if you need to. Until a couple of hours in, when you get auto-aim weapons. At that point just spin in circles to avoid getting hit, while automatically clearing the screen in seconds. What is disappointing is how easily this could have been fixed. As other games in the genre have done, add strafe or reverse thrust, scale down the player's strength, and make shooting cost energy or overheat or overwise have something to limit the rate of fire. This would have made combat engaging, challenging, and skill based rather than just based on who can tank damage longer. This could then have been one or my favorite games, as the story and world are otherwise engaging enough to keep me playing.

This is an extremely fun game with HIGH replayability. I have always enjoyed it, and you probably will, too. Give it a shot, you won't regret it.

A brilliant yet flawed game. In development for well over 20 years now, and it shows in both positive and negative ways.

The game is expansive, with tons of ships, weapons, items, factions etc. On the other hand, There is little explicit plot tying these together. There are only a handful of explicit missions to follow.

There are many systems, and some of them are quite large. On the other hand, systems start out unexplored and unless you have a mapping item it's a real pain to trek across a large map hoping to find POIs. Doing this over and over gets repetitive.

There are several factions you can join and climb the ranks of, by completing randomly generated missions. On the other hand, because of the randomness, you might not find enough of these missions to progress and therefore be stuck.

The galaxy is large but feels static. Trade resources generally do not replenish, and stations eventually stop buying certain items. As a result, once you're done with a system, there is no money to be made, you generally have no reason to go back there, and it's effectively dead to you. I get this is a reason to continue pushing forward, but it would be nice to have a more lively game.

A full playthrough will take you many hours, a lot of it repetitive. On the other hand, there is a certain satisfaction in slowly upgrading your ship from a leaky rustbucket to an impenetrable killing machine able to solo enemy fleets.

I would recommend playing the base campaign (for free!) first to see whether you want to pony up for the expansions.

An ambitious sci-fi rougelike with a lot of soul! Crazy coming back to this after at least 15 years and seeing how much has changed.

Pros
- A fascinating and well-written setting with a lot of mystery that I felt compelled to explore further and further into.
- Screenshots don't quite do it justice but this game looks great in motion. Art design is great too with the blocky Commonwealth ships, sleek designs of the Ares Orthodoxy and plenty of other bizarre and striking visuals for the more alien factions.
- Lots of hidden mechanics to figure out through trial and error.
- Great freedom. You can go around building making an honest living as an escort (.. not like that) for shipping corporations or spend your time smuggling drugs, human organs and (worst of all) pirated movies. Or whatever the hell you want! There's many paths to power and thankfully no need for grinding due to the XP-less system.
- It's an awesome feeling turning your ship from some little flea equipped with an ancient engine and a peashooter into some crazy end-game nuclear missile flinging, time-stopping behemoth.

Cons
- Some of the UI is starting to show its age a bit. Sorting through your inventory becomes quite the pain by mid-game, especially without the ability to sort by categories.
- I use fuel even when parked??? I think I got so interested in reading item descriptions once I spent half a tank of fuel. Does this guy just leave the ship idling for a month or something?

It's not the worst game in the world, by any stretch. But.

- It runs at 30 fps and that fps is tied to the animations etc, so it's stuck there permanently
- The keybinds are horrid, and though it may be possible to edit them via an xml file, it's not populated by default so you'd need to know the correct parameters. In-game keybind config simply does not work.
- There is no options menu. No way to turn down the music (just off), no way to change resolution, screen mode, graphics, nothing. For a game 20 years in development, yeah I expected more here.
- This shouldn't be a negative, but it feels like the game Tyrian except you can go in all directions. Enemy space stations are easily dispatched with your starter ship, and enemy ships are mostly just cannon fodder and die in one or two hits. I guess the game was originally intended as a roguelike - it shows.
- As far as I've seen, there's only one active weapon slot pr ship, no matter how big it is. Boring.
- The whole fuel system is terrible. Fuel seems to get spent even if you are docked - that's just bad design. It gets better later on with fuel efficiency and larger reactors, but with apparently no way of fuel scooping (there was one, but the dev removed it), it will always be an annoyance.

[h1]Overview[/h1]
So just based on the time I played this and might play in the future you might be confused why I am trying to discourage others from playing it. This is because the core gameplay loop game can be fun but the game overall is just not great.

So first what it is good at: [b] This game is an isometric space combat simulator, with a significant amount of different weapons and defense configurations that are well balanced.[/b] Your core gameplay loop is entering a star system, flying around to different space stations to trade primarily scrapped weapons and usually get a single mission. Then you complete the mission by usually destroying or defending a target. After that you search for other enemy bases to destroy and loot to sell the drops at one of the friendly bases. The resulting cash will be used for better weapons or armor, ammo or - especially in the first half of a run - huge amounts of fuel. Then you leave towards the next star system and rinse repeat.

The game is probably fun for you (like it was for me) if you like clearing out maps of enemies entirely or scour the universe to find your perfect weapon configuration, but apart from what I wrote before, there is not much else to do.

[h1]Weaknesses[/h1]
[h3]Outdated[/h3]
This game has been in development for 20 years by a dedicated developer, which is cool but also comes with a certain level of outdatedness. A very clear example are the settings, which consist of of a mod overview, a button for turning music on and off and the key bindings. The key bindings are kind of unique but can be changed. They include something like "sound lower" and "sound louder", which is the only way of changing effect volume (music volume is unaffected by this and can only be turned off). This age of everything is also noticeable in game play (not polygon based but sprite based graphics e.g.).
[h3]Inventory issues[/h3]
The inventory management is so annoying that it makes me wish back the old school diablo pages where you had to play tetris to fit stuff in. You literally just have a list of stuff, which can become 10-20 pages long, that you can not sort or filter. The pain when selling anything specific (which will happen constantly) results in maybe a fifth of the play time just spent on inventory management as you pick up an insane amount of useless stuff. This is worsened by the majority of ships having enough cargo to maybe loot one late game enemy camp before returning to sell, which is fun if there are 20 enemy camps in a map and the next buyer is 2 maps away.
[h3]Cool ideas but not fleshed out well[/h3]
There is technically more content in this game than destroy enemy bases, loot, sell, upgrade ship, rinse repeat. All of it feels like it would have needed more attention though:
You can change to other star ships but there is basically no progression in that area, while different ships have different strenghts you could easily finish with the starting ship you chose without missing out.
There is technically mining in the game and it is possible to make it profitable, but it is extremely time consuming and generally lackluster, which means you are discouraged from actually doing it.
The aforementioned missions let you rank up in different factions, which is a great start, but for some reason you get at best one per station. That means all the rank progression inevitably stalls unless you get a lucky seed that actually creates enough stations to reach the highest rank for that faction.
There is also technically a story that binds in the super powers you get (which kind of ♥♥♥♥ up late game balance but that's fine imo). However, the entire story consists of like 10 conversations of at best a page of text so I'd argue that it is not that relevant. It is also only part one of a story that is set up to take 3 parts to be told so take that how you will.

I think even though the successor is already in the works this one is also still developed so hopefully in less than another 20 years this will have everything on a level that I could call it a good game.

[h1] It started well, but ended badly. [/h1]

When you begin the game, you will be greeted with cool ships which 90% of them you can buy and customize, cool text quests with interesting lore, basic fun combat mechanics with some twists (different types of damage, different weapon behavior and etc.) and some nice side activities.

After playing for a while, you might think, 'This game is awesome! I want to see more!', but you will be disappointed. You will get more generated quest like "kill that" "destroy this base" "protect this" and less quests with some interesting backstory. All the activities such as mining, smuggling and trading will degenerate into mindless combat. Even combat itself will worsen as you are thrown at more and stronger enemies with less to no room to improve your ship. UI/UX is mediocre at best: cargo screen has no filters and it's hard to navigate, no text log if you accidently skip dialog, no list of ROM(basically some minor upgrades to your ship) improvement, bad key rebinding menu and so on. Your wingman AI will just stoically accept death from radiation and you can’t do anything about it, as you can't customise their ship or anything.

This downhill trend also can be seen in quests. You will encounter more bugs and poor mission design.  You can softlock yourself if you decide to start mission 8th in the Benedict & Fiona arc later.  In the final mission you need to complete some generic missions from research stations, but they will be attack and you won’t have time to complete the missions and to defend the stations.

Challenge mode is very difficult and was the base difficulty prior to v1.9 which seems to be the reason for some negative reviews. It took me ~6 deaths to be okay and not die immediately. 

Some old but top review state you cannot switch ships. This is false. While you cannot capture ships, you can get little helper drones which can act as cargo ships, scouts, point defense, etc. 

Some mechanics are not as clear as they should be.

If you get hit my a toxic/radioactive missile, you need to get to a station equipped with dock services asap. You will be charged ~480 credits to decon. 

The UI seems bare at first but after destroying stations you'll find upgrades which make things more apparent.
If you can forgive the clunky UI (which nevertheless continues to be improved upon) it has considerable depth for a game that continues to build 15 years onwards.
